A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LaSM. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised and added content despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendix B.3 report original defense evaluations, scaling ablations and AndroidControl episode results.

after.justification: Sections 5–6 and supplementary Sections 8–9 report original defense evaluations, including backbone comparisons, coefficient sweeps, position tests and failure analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same joint attention/MLP parameter scaling, Equation 3 and progressive layer-range narrowing. The added coefficient-selection discussion elaborates hyperparameter tuning; it does not establish a different defense mechanism.

E1.justification: Both retain 200 base screenshots expanded into 2,400 perturbations and the AndroidControl evaluation of 224 episodes. V2 adds explicit spatial variation through top, middle and bottom pop-up conditions in Section 8.5. The multi-step task itself already appeared in v1 Appendix B.3.

E2.justification: The standalone comparator set remains No Defense, DPO, Direct Alert and CoT Alert. V2 Table 1 additionally reports DPO+LaSM and Direct Alert+LaSM combinations; v1 Tables 1–2 reported LaSM alone and CoT+LaSM but lacked those two combinations.

E3.justification: V2 substantially extends evaluation configurations through two additional backbones, GELab-Zero-4B and MAI-UI-8B, a denser two-model coefficient sweep and controlled position tests. It also changes the stated Type metric from typing accuracy to action-type exact match. FESR becomes TSR with the same episode-success meaning, and the original 224-episode construction remains.

E4.justification: V2 expands the four-value coefficient analysis into a two-model sweep, adds controlled position robustness tests and presents two failure modes involving minimal interfaces and text input. The original component ablation and hidden-state analysis remain; v1 Figure 7 is relocated as v2 Figure 12 rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both provide point estimates and sample averages. V2 Table 1's arrows describe performance differences after applying LaSM, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Central results are extensively replaced. Qwen overlay averages for No Defense/LaSM change from 39.3/74.8 in v1 Table 1 to 18.9/66.4 in v2 Table 1. LLaVA CoT+LaSM overlay/inductive averages change from 100/100 to 86.9/90.3. V2 also adds combination, backbone, coefficient and position results. These are reported result replacements, not established same-setting performance changes, because the versions do not fully reconcile their experimental conditions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same attention-patch, cosine-similarity, scaling-update and attention-averaging mathematics. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs. The revised empirical Type metric does not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central training-free defense claim remains. V2 replaces the contribution emphasizing at least 98% combined-defense DSR with a 61.92% relative episode-success improvement derived from retained results, and qualifies performance preservation as minimal impact. Its introduction also newly claims standalone LLaVA LaSM reaches 100%, which conflicts with v2 Table 1.

C2.justification: V2 revises the visual-saliency explanation from broadly harmful prominence to model-dependent effects. Sections 8.2 and 8.4–8.6 add substantive discussion of controlled CoT evaluation, benign pop-ups, the DSR–TSR gap and failure mechanisms. Conversely, v1's explicit limitations concerning preliminary interpretability and lack of physical-device evaluation are omitted.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link, model-specific scaling coefficients and a stated 0.05 tuning increment. Section 9.3 newly explains OS-Atlas official action/coordinate prompting and target-region scoring. These improve documented reproducibility information without establishing changes to all previously evaluated settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds three cited works: LLM for Mobile, the OS Agents survey and Agent-ScanKit. The latter supports a new connection between failure cases and memorization versus reasoning. The existing GUI-agent, injection-attack and saliency-method positioning otherwise remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: The introduction and main-results narrative are substantially rewritten, Section 6 is reorganized, and supplementary discussion precedes implementation details instead of following them. The hidden-state discussion moves from the main text to Section 8.7. Author information and acknowledgments also expand.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout and merges the two main result tables into a combined table with baseline, post-LaSM and difference values. Heatmap and screenshot examples are replaced or redesigned, new coefficient/position/failure displays are added, and existing prompt boxes become separately captioned full-page figures.

improvement.justification: The added position tests, failure analyses, coefficient studies and code link improve evidence and usability. However, v2 introduces material reporting conflicts: its introduction claims standalone LLaVA achieves 100%, whereas Table 1 reports averages of 81.2% and 78.0%; Section 6.2 retains DPO's v1 score of 1.42%, while Table 1 reports 52.3%. The unexplained replacement of central results and omission of the physical-device limitation counterbalance the useful additions, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
